Private external debt is the stock of outstanding debt owed by the private sector of a country to nonresidents. It covers the obligations of private corporations, financial institutions and households, including loans, bonds and other financial liabilities denominated in foreign or domestic currency when the creditors are abroad. This indicator reflects the external borrowing of the private sector and its exposure to foreign financial risks. The definition may vary by country.
